newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Presidency puts forward new proposal to open gas markets.
newsitem.headline: Presidency puts forward new proposal to open gas markets.

text.p: The Irish presidency has put forward a new compromise text on liberalising European Union gas markets, diplomats said on Wednesday.
The 90-page document will be discussed for the first time on Monday and Tuesday in the Council's energy working group, they said.
"It will be the working basis for the work in Council," said one diplomat. The diplomats declined to comment on the content of the proposal, saying they had not yet had time to study it.
However, one diplomat forecast difficult talks ahead, adding it would be "more than optimistic" to believe there would be an agreement already during the Dutch presidency.
Another diplomat said the Irish presidency had sought to pick up some technological solutions from the agreement on electricity market liberalisation of last June.
However, there were also wide differences between the two sectors, diplomats said.

France, sceptical of far-reaching liberalisation, had for example not launched its idea at the electricity talks of introducing a single buyer system as an option alongside the system of negotiated third party access to national grids.
The new text builds on discussions by EU energy officials earlier this autumn on the amended Commission proposal on the internal market in natural gas, COM(93)643.
That proposal was put forward already in 1993 but was left in abeyance while the EU focused on the twin directive on electricity.
The 1993 proposal said the liberalisation of the gas markets should be implemented in phases "in order to enable industry to adjust in a flexible and ordered manner to its new environment."
Diplomats hope some aspects of the electricity deal, which foresees a gradual and limited liberalisation, can be used for natural gas, removing some potential obstacles.
